First of all, this review is from a singleplayer standpoint and directed towards newcomers to this game. I tried playing in a server once last year, and absolutely hated the experience. The PVP element seems to be mainly why this game has gotten so many negative reviews. But instead of getting stomped all over in the servers by the trolls & alpha tribes, if any of you are interested in playing by yourself or on LAN, read on!

All I heard about this game when it first came out was that it was really poorly optimised and in early access. So I avoided it like the plague. Until last year, when I started watching Let's Plays on Youtube, and I fell in love. It still is the game I play the most out of all my games. Last week I tamed a T-rex for the first time. It felt awesome. Yes there is so much grind, and yes I do have all the XP/taming rates turned up, and it still is a grind. But damn, it's a fun grind. And I learned so much about dinosaurs in the process! It makes the inner dino-obsessed little girl in me so happy :)

You start out naked and alone, and with tools you craft yourself you slowly build up a base. Location is everything. In the north, the cold and large carnivores will defeat you very quickly. But in the south, the weather is milder and the dinos are not so big and scary. Taming dinos is fun and frightening, and often frustrating but it makes the grind a lot easier as different dinos help you to gather different materials with ease and of course help protect you. I used to wonder what the point of this game is; you grind to get better gear, and then you grind some more. But if you enjoy the grind and being scared out of your wits most of the time, then you will love this game and get a very rewarding experience out of it. 

But it still is very brutal. Sometimes you spend so long taming something, or building a base, only to die and lose it all in an instant. Be prepared to be very very frustrated, it definitely is one of the most challenging games I have ever played. The original Island map is fun and massive to explore, but the free Center expansion map is even bigger and much more beautiful and varied.

There are caves you can explore underwater and the devs are adding more and more aggressive water dinos that make it very challenging and rewarding to explore the seas. If you make it to end game, there are several artifacts you can loot in dangerous caves you have to fight your way out of, and there are bosses you can summon & take on for very big rewards. You can take your time, and gather & build, or you can take out the big guns, level up, tame high tier dinos, expand and technologically improve your base. There is an insane amount you can do, and you can play it your way without being restricted by a linear storyline.

Now on to some cons, it is super glitchy sometimes. The worst one is when you get stuck on knocked out dinos, or rocks, or in doors, or.. really anything. It is frustrating and sometimes all you can really do to fix it is to wait it out, break the rock you are stuck in (if you're lucky), or log out & log back in again (which takes forever for me). This doesn't happen often but when it does, it is very irritating. It is also a common sight to see wild dinos stuck in trees, which makes taming them easy & cheat-y. Though some of the weird graphic glitches can actually be quite funny :) Another thing I dislike about this game is the building mechanics. It is not intuitive at all, and sometimes you can't build or place certain items "because Ark". This means that you frequently have to tear down what you have built, which ends up costing you half the materials you used to make it.

And the other thing I really dislike about this is the fact that the game is STILL in early access. I was very disappointed when the devs made the Scorched Earth map a paid DLC. Not that it isn't fun to play, it really is - but I felt like they really should have finished the main game first before making DLCs. There is a new minor update almost every time I play this game, which is a bit annoying as you have to download it every time - but all that they seem to be doing recently are adding more and more interesting & slightly OP dinos, which is great, but makes some of the older dino models now obsolete. I really wish they would focus more on ironing out all the little problems with the base game rather than adding more and more new dinos. I would love to also see some new and varied character designs & more in depth customisation on the way your character looks & sounds (the devs are now sponsoring mod makers to develop their mods, which I think is great news for Ark).

Even after all these flaws, I still keep coming back for more. If you love survival games, exploring, crafting, building, gardening, breeding (!), fighting, and let's not forget - if you have any sort of interest in dinosaurs, you will love this game. Make sure you have a good PC to run this and start taming! Prepare to throw away a whole lot of hours on this as it is damn addictive :)

After a single mounted saber tooth destroyed my tribes house and all of our belongings, I decided it was time to head out and be a nomad. Fully expecting to die on this journey, I didn't pay attention to where I was going, but took off. The first night consisted of making myself some armor and tools. After crafting a spear and collecting all the meet I could carry, I was off. The first day was a roller coster of emotions and close calls as I roamed the island from supply drop to supply drop. With each new loot box, I became more powerful and cautiously optimistic that this would work out. I found myself well armed and starving atop a mountain with a few parachutes I had just collected.
I did the only logical thing and dove off the mountain, soaring across a ravine and past brontosaurs like a scene from jurassic park. I landed next to another supply drop, and to my surprise, found the makings of a decent wooden house.
With the ability to make a small abode, I decided traveling alone had gotten lonely, so i used my bow and tranq arrows to take down a small dilo, that would be named Mr. Spitter. Life was good, we traveled together and became close friends. Mr. Spitter had my back and I had his, but all of my gear had gotten too heavy, and the little dilo couldn't help much. It was time for a mount.
The only mount of choice for a wander in this game is the raptor, its speed and lethality make it a perfect traveling companion. with some time and hunting, I brought down a raptor and tamed it slowly. So slowly, im fact, that I got Mr. Spitter a mate, and hunted with them while my raptor was tamed. I returned to the raptor just before he became a loyal companion to place my new forged saddle on him and rode off into the sun.
Usually this would be the happy ending, but in all survivor games like this one, there is no happy ending. Either you quit while you're content, or you live long enough to see everything taken from you. My new family and i traveled together until I found a supply drop under water. With the loot pulling me forward like a moth to a flame, I dove in the river and my trusty companions followed me in. Little did I know what lurked beneath the surface. Piranha swarmed us and devoured Mr. Spitter alive before I could even react. I pulled out my spear just in time for my second dilo to die. I couldn't let Speedy, my raptor, suffer the same fate. In a flurry of thrusts, I managed to save Speedy by a hair. The loot that laid inside contained the remaining pieces i needed for a house. 
Filled with sorrow, I decided it was time to head home and rebuild a base for my tribe, but I soon realized I was lost. Speedy and I roamed for hours searching for landmarks to guide us home. I finally found the path home and eagerly followed the beach along the river to where I could rest for the night. Speedy was tired from running, and we were both to the limits of what we could bare to carry. I decided to give speedy a break and jump off, just to luckily find a stegosaraus egg. I thought it would be nice to return to the tribe with another dinosaur that we could all hatch and train together. I didn't notice the two large dinodaurs who were watching the egg closely, and didn't appreciate a stranger taking their young. THey were on me before I could draw my weapon. I had over encumbered myself, and Speedy counldn't move. I died slowly trying to drop the egg, and received the final blow as i attemted to join speedy to make my get away. My wishful thinking turned to greed, and lead to dispair. I awoke at the shambles of our base, naked and alone, with nothing left to show for my time on the island.

After spending over 700 hours and nearly five years with ARK, I can say without hesitation that this game has left a real mark on me. It’s chaotic, it’s challenging, and it can be downright frustrating. But it’s also incredibly rewarding, and that’s what has kept me coming back.

The taming system is what hooked me from the start. No other game I've played lets you bond with creatures in the way ARK does. Whether it’s your very first Parasaur or that hard-earned high-level Rex you tracked for what felt like forever, every tame feels meaningful. 

I’ve always loved the progression in this game. Starting out with nothing but a stone pick in your hand and slowly working your way up to full Tek gear and a powerful dino army… there's nothing quite like it. I enjoy games where effort pays off, and ARK delivers with its grind, farming, and patience-rewarding gameplay.

The soundtrack is genuinely beautiful. The music captures the wonder and danger of each environment in a way that sticks with you long after you log off.

That said, I do think it’s a shame that ARK: Evolved has been left behind in favor of ARK: Ascended. While Ascended might offer visual upgrades, I’m sticking with Evolved. It’s the version that I, and many others, built our memories in, and I still wholeheartedly recommend it to new players who want that original, raw survival experience.

Is it perfect? Definitely not. You’ll run into bugs, crashes, and the occasional rage-quit moment. But that’s just part of ARK’s charm. It may not be the most polished game, but it has heart. 
If you enjoy survival games with depth, creativity, and meaningful progression, ARK: Survival Evolved is something truly special.
